notes:
POC objective: validate Dedicated capacity for low-latency, high-throughput inference for customer-facing trading assistants and re-ranking of signals. Primary success metrics:
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for chat-style prompts under normal load; p50 target < 80ms.
- Throughput: sustained 1.2M tokens/hour (post-quantization) for peak trading window; burst to 2.5M tokens/hour.
- Reliability: 99.9% availability during trading hours; graceful fallback to lower-cost model when GPU pressure >85%.
- Cost profile: unit cost per 1k tokens must be < 30% above their current on-prem spend for comparable latency.

POC scope & plan (8-week):
- Week 0: SOW & infra kickoff, access + network setup (VPC peering, KMS).
- Week 1-2: Baseline ingestion & model onboarding (customer will bring two model families: a trimmed Llama variant + a 7B quantized model).
- Week 3: Synthetic load tests (ramp tests) — tool: Redwood load harness + k6 scripts. Ramp schedule: 0->10%->25%->50%->100% over 8 hours.
- Week 4: Soak test — 72-hour sustained at 80% of target throughput, collect memory/KV metrics, cache hit rates.
- Week 5: Representative prompt suite (customer-provided & Redwood-curated) — 5k requests across chat, rerank, embeddings.
- Week 6: Failure injection & fallback validation — simulate node OOM, network partition, cold cache warmup.
- Week 7: SLA verification & runbook validation; measure tail latencies under mixed workloads.
- Week 8: Security review closeout, exec demo, handoff to ops + CSM (if purchase proceeds).

Representative prompts (examples):
- Chat (trading assistant): 'Summarize order book delta for X in last 5 minutes; highlight anomalous fills.'
- Rerank: 50 query-document pairs with short context; goal: p95 latency < 120ms for rerank calls at 50 qps.
- Embeddings: batch 10k small documents (avg 120 tokens) for nightly index refresh; target throughput 500 embeds/sec.

Infrastructure ask / Reserved GPU planning:
- Initial reserved pool proposal: 8 x A100-80GB (or 6 x H100 depending on availability) with headroom for burst to 12 GPUs via burst pool.
- Autoscaling policy: keep 25% idle headroom during trading windows; aggressive scale-in outside windows.
- KV / prefix cache enabled to reduce repeated generation costs (expect 15-25% token savings on chat flows).

SLA negotiation points surfaced by legal/procurement:
- Request: 99.95% uptime during configured trading hours; Redwood standard is 99.9% — legal asking for credit formula for p95/p99 latency misses.
- Data residency: require logs and full audit trail stored in region (us-east-1) for 7 years.
- Incident communications: 15 min paging for Sev1 during trading hours.

Open questions (for Redwood SE & CSM):
- Can we provide a validated p95 latency SLO for the customer's exact model family at 8-GPU reserved capacity? Need benchmark run.
- Need a concrete cost model: cost/kgpu-hour + expected token unit cost at target throughput.
- How does fallback to hosted variants affect compliance? Customer wants encrypted KMS keys for any transit.

Decision signals:
- Positive: If soak test shows p95 < 220ms and throughput within 10% of target and security QA clears, they will move to 12-month reserved capacity.
- Negative: If tail latencies exceed SLO under simulated burst or legal cannot accept 99.9% contractual uptime, deal stalls.

Stenographic notes / quotes: "Performance is non-negotiable during trading hours — we need near real-time answers or the product is useless" — Head of ML (Wyvern).

Internal actions (Redwood):
- SE to provision benchmark harness and run initial 24-hour stress test by 2026-03-12.
- Contracts team to prepare a variant SLO addendum (99.95 request) and submit to Wyvern legal.
- Security: prepare KMS integration checklist and residency addendum.

Attachments: performance test template, sample prompt CSV, draft SOW (see drive links).
